Preparation burden evidenced: Modified-Hummers GO oxidation; concentrated H2SO4, KMnO4, H2O2 and HCl washes; alginate/CaCl2 fiber formation; ultrasound and vacuum freeze-drying; yield and energy unreported.
Separation / recovery route: Fibrous immobilized format; separation route not developed into a quantified recovery process in the article.
Regeneration / repeated use: No adsorption–desorption or repeated-use cycles reported.
Water-matrix / operating evidence: Batch synthetic aqueous TC; pH and concentration tests; no real-water or column validation in the extracted article.
Cost evidence actually available: No quantified cost, yield, freeze-drying energy or cost per mass TC removed; “environmentally friendly/low-cost alginate” is not a process calculation.
Feasibility assessment / key unresolved: Immobilization may aid handling, but synthesis and freeze-drying burden is uncosted and reuse has not been demonstrated.

Preparation burden evidenced: Electronic-waste graphite recovery/cleaning; concentrated-acid/oxidant GO route; Fe salts, CMC, NaOH; 85°C treatment and 18 h vacuum drying.
Regeneration / repeated use: Methanol regeneration; ten cycles reportedly decrease removal from ~96% to ~92%.
Water-matrix / operating evidence: Low-concentration synthetic aqueous TC tests; no normalized real-wastewater cost comparison.
Cost evidence actually available: No total cost/energy inventory; authors’ “cost-effective” claim not monetized. Methanol purchase, recovery and disposal not costed.
Feasibility assessment / key unresolved: Magnetic recovery and ten-cycle result are practical positives, but upstream graphite purification/GO synthesis and methanol handling need full cost boundary.

Preparation burden evidenced: Modified-Hummers GO; magnetite synthesis; paper fibrillation with NaOH/NaClO/H2SO4; 360 W ultrasonication; 48 h lyophilization; yield and energy cost absent.
Regeneration / repeated use: Five adsorption–desorption cycles; removal drops from 88.33% to 75.38%.
Water-matrix / operating evidence: Synthetic aqueous TC batch tests; no real-water study reported in the extraction.
Cost evidence actually available: No quantified cost inventory; waste-paper precursor is not proof of low total cost.
Feasibility assessment / key unresolved: Magnetic handling is demonstrated, but chemical treatment and freeze-drying are substantial uncosted process steps; cycle decline is material.

Preparation burden evidenced: Spent Zn–C battery carbon rods cleaned and acid-treated; HCl/HNO3 pretreatment, H2SO4/H3PO4/KMnO4 oxidation, H2O2 quench, repeated acid/water/ethanol washing and multiple drying stages.
Separation / recovery route: Powder separation by centrifugation/filtration in batch; practical large-scale separation not tested.
Water-matrix / operating evidence: Synthetic aqueous CIP batch; no real-water validation identified in primary full text.
Cost evidence actually available: No yield, reagent cost, energy, washing-waste or normalized cost. “Economical” is author wording only.
Feasibility assessment / key unresolved: Waste precursor availability is a possible supply advantage, but hazardous pretreatment/oxidation and drying remain; inconsistent dose and removal/uptake values further limit performance claims.

Preparation burden evidenced: Multi-stage GO oxidation, P-doping, TETA grafting, EDC/NHS coupling, β-cyclodextrin acrylation in DMF/triethylamine/acryloyl chloride, hydrogel polymerization at 75°C and washing/drying.
Separation / recovery route: Hydrogel network provides an immobilized form; detailed large-scale separation/recovery costs not measured.
Regeneration / repeated use: Seven methanol adsorption–desorption cycles; about 90.53% of original removal retained after cycle seven.
Water-matrix / operating evidence: CIP batch tests and Cu2+ co-adsorption; figure/application matrix label says simulated real wastewater, while prose says real-water samples.
Cost evidence actually available: No quantified synthesis cost, yield, energy, chemical recovery or normalized cost per CIP removed.
Feasibility assessment / key unresolved: High reported fitted/validated uptake does not offset the multi-step reagent burden. Matrix identity and validation solution volume remain caveats.

Preparation burden evidenced: Modified-Hummers oxidation with concentrated acids and 18 g KMnO4 per 3 g graphite, extensive washing and diethyl ether; yield/cost not reported.
Separation / recovery route: Powder recovery/washing between cycles; not a magnetic format.
Regeneration / repeated use: DMF + 1 M HCl elution; >99.14% release within 240 min; five cycles retain >95.78% of initial capacity (reported). Drying at 100°C before reuse.
Water-matrix / operating evidence: Synthetic single-solute aqueous CIP; cation effects tested; no real wastewater.
Cost evidence actually available: No quantified production cost, solvent/acid recovery, energy or cost per mass removed. DMF/HCl regeneration burden is not priced.
Feasibility assessment / key unresolved: Good reported cycle retention, but regeneration is solvent/acid intensive and no solvent recovery or waste treatment boundary is reported.

Configuration / target: N-rGO — TC in six-antibiotic trace mixture
Preparation burden evidenced: Strong-acid/oxidant GO oxidation; 100 W ultrasonication; ammonia-assisted hydrothermal N-doping at 180°C for 24 h; washing/drying; no yield or reagent recovery.
Separation / recovery route: Powder adsorbent; 0.1 M HCl elution and 0.1 M NaOH regeneration, then DI washing.
Regeneration / repeated use: Up to eight cycles; authors state capacity decrease no more than 25%.
Water-matrix / operating evidence: Trace-level multi-antibiotic tests; 100 mmol/L ion interference tests and 0.5–10 mg/L humic-acid tests; HA at 10 mg/L reduced uptake up to 30%.
Cost evidence actually available: No energy, yield, chemical-recovery, eluate-treatment or cost denominator.
Feasibility assessment / key unresolved: Potential trace-level application and repeat-use evidence, but strong process burden and unresolved concentration/volume basis plus fitted-qm concerns remain.

Preparation burden evidenced: Graphene production/preparation not exposed in accessible abstract; do not infer manufacturing burden from the treatment test.
Separation / recovery route: Abstract notes graphene separation/recovery is necessary; no quantified recovery route in accessible text.
Regeneration / repeated use: No multi-cycle regeneration evidence confirmed in the abstract.
Water-matrix / operating evidence: Publisher abstract reports tests with ionic strength, 5 mg/L NOM and river/drinking-water sources; exact conditions and effect sizes are not exposed.
Cost evidence actually available: No quantified production/recovery cost, yield, reagent/energy inventory or cost boundary.
Feasibility assessment / key unresolved: Potentially useful matrix benchmark, but full text is needed for process and cost assessment; GAC remains benchmark only.

Preparation burden evidenced: CNF/GO dispersion; stated 1000 W ultrasonic output; freeze >5 h; vacuum freeze-dry 48 h at −55°C; upstream CNF/GO costs not included.
Separation / recovery route: Monolithic aerogel recovered from solution and separated before washing.
Regeneration / repeated use: 5 wt.% NaOH for 5 h; ten cycles; TC removal 82.1% initially to 78.9% after cycle ten; wash and freeze-dry between cycles.
Water-matrix / operating evidence: Synthetic batch tests; multi-antibiotic screen; Fig. 7 condition label is incomplete; no actual wastewater matrix validated in the cited result.
Cost evidence actually available: No production cost, yield, energy per mass, GO input cost or NaOH consumption/disposal cost; “economical” is not a TEA.
Feasibility assessment / key unresolved: Immobilized aerogel and ten-cycle retention are operational advantages, but high-output sonication, long freeze-drying and alkaline regeneration are uncosted.

Configuration / target: Graphene — TC in seven-antibiotic trace mixture
Preparation burden evidenced: Graphene synthesis not reproduced; synthesis is cited to earlier work. This article reports washing, freeze-drying and UV treatment but no material yield.
Separation / recovery route: Graphene separated in analytical batch workflow; scalable recovery is not demonstrated.
Water-matrix / operating evidence: Synthetic seven-antibiotic mixture at 200 μg/L per drug, pH 7, 298 K, 1 g/L; TC uptake reached equilibrium in ~2.5 h.
Cost evidence actually available: No quantified graphene synthesis cost, yield, energy, chemical inputs or mass-removed denominator; “cheap” label not a cost analysis.
Feasibility assessment / key unresolved: Strong low-concentration mixed-solute context, but no reuse, real-water demonstration or graphene manufacturing inventory.

Preparation burden evidenced: Waste dry-cell graphite cleaned with Aqua Regia; improved-Hummers acids/KMnO4/H2O2; cobalt/iron salts; pH adjustment to ~10; heating and ethanol/water washing; yield not reported.
Regeneration / repeated use: Methanol regeneration and drying at 50°C; up to eight rounds; overall removal reportedly decreases ~95% to ~90% (not a TC-specific per-cycle series).
Water-matrix / operating evidence: TC-specific synthetic-water test at 0.2 mg/L, pH 7, 30 s; no actual water-matrix test reported.
Cost evidence actually available: No monetized cost, product yield, energy or chemical recovery. Waste-derived graphite does not establish low total cost.
Feasibility assessment / key unresolved: Rapid low-concentration removal and magnetic separation are promising, but cost, yield and real-water performance remain unproven.

Configuration / target: Fe3O4/rGO with rotating magnetic field — TCH
Preparation burden evidenced: Publisher preview confirms co-precipitated Fe3O4/rGO variant but exact recipe, precursor ratio and yield are inaccessible.
Separation / recovery route: Magnetic composite and rotating-field operation; practical recovery and field hardware not fully disclosed in preview.
Regeneration / repeated use: >87% removal efficiency retained after four cycles; regenerant and reuse protocol unavailable.
Water-matrix / operating evidence: Publisher preview claims coexisting-ion/complex-water tests but matrix composition/results are not accessible; TCH is distinct from OFL.
Cost evidence actually available: No energy or cost inventory. A 2 A excitation current alone is not power or energy per volume; voltage, resistance, field strength/frequency and duty cycle unavailable.
Feasibility assessment / key unresolved: Do not claim energy-efficiency or low-cost superiority until complete operational energy, field conditions and recovery data are available.

Configuration / target: Sulfonated GO — multi-FQ mixtures containing CIP
Preparation burden evidenced: Strong-acid/oxidant Hummers oxidation, sulfonation, ethanol/diethyl-ether washes; no yield or solvent recovery.
Separation / recovery route: Powder batch separation; solvent desorption required.
Regeneration / repeated use: DMF + 1 M HCl; >97% release within 10 min; five cycles retain >92% at the mixture level.
Water-matrix / operating evidence: Equimolar binary/ternary/quaternary synthetic FQ solutions; article explicitly states no real wastewater testing.
Cost evidence actually available: No cost per mass removed, reagent/solvent recovery or energy. Mixture q_e/q_m cannot be attributed to CIP alone.
Feasibility assessment / key unresolved: Useful competition and reuse study, but mixture totals are not CIP-specific and regeneration has hazardous-solvent/acid burdens.

Configuration / target: GO/alginate hydrogel beads as CIP PRB media
Preparation burden evidenced: Publisher abstract confirms bead synthesis but detailed formulation, crosslinker ratios, washing, drying and yield were inaccessible.
Separation / recovery route: PRB backfill/immobilized bead concept; flow-through tests were described in abstract but column dimensions, flow and breakthrough tables unavailable.
Regeneration / repeated use: No batch regeneration/reuse cycles reported; PRB service life is a separate operational metric.
Water-matrix / operating evidence: Groundwater PRB remediation described; no field-scale validation or numerical breakthrough series verified.

Feasibility assessment / key unresolved: Conceptually relevant continuous-flow application, but source access prevents independent cost/column verification; do not treat service life as regeneration.

Preparation burden evidenced: Modified-Hummers GO oxidation; 9.8 g KMnO4 per 1 g graphite in stated recipe, prolonged drying, PVA/alginate dissolution and sonication; boric acid/CaCl2 curing for 12 h.
Separation / recovery route: Beads recovered by filtration/centrifugation in batch; no magnetic separation.
Regeneration / repeated use: Authors claim 4–5 cycles with <25% capacity loss using acid/alkali; cycle-specific series not independently pinned.
Water-matrix / operating evidence: Synthetic aqueous CIP only; no real wastewater. Experimentally used bead dose 0.5 g/50 mL (10 g/L) for a key result.
Cost evidence actually available: Author estimate $10–30/kg bead; cost calculation assumes 0.1 g/L, 100× below the stated 10 g/L experimental loading. No traceable cost worksheet, yield or energy inventory.
Feasibility assessment / key unresolved: Only candidate with a nominal unit cost, but the 100-fold dose mismatch and missing cost worksheet make its <$ per removed antibiotic claim non-reproducible.

Preparation burden evidenced: Battery-derived graphite purification (including aqua-regia); improved-Hummers GO; Fe salts for m-GO; cobalt nitrate/2-methylimidazole Co-MOF in methanol; composite assembly, solvent washes and 60°C vacuum drying. Yield and energy unreported.
Regeneration / repeated use: Methanol regeneration; 10 cycles, reported removal decreases about 98%→91%.
Water-matrix / operating evidence: Experiments use ultrapure DI water. No real-water, competing-ion or humic-acid tests located in full text.
Cost evidence actually available: No product yield, cost, chemical recovery, energy, methanol recovery or cost per volume treated/mass removed.
Feasibility assessment / key unresolved: Waste battery graphite is a feedstock advantage but does not establish low cost: purification, oxidation, Co-MOF synthesis and solvent washing are uncosted. No real-water validation; kinetic qe and fitted qm require caveats.
